channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan Outlines Transport Priorities at Seoul Conference
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Transport, Azim Ibrohim, presented the country's transport infrastructure and international connectivity priorities at the GICC 2026 conference in Seoul. He emphasized the importance of modern, reliable transport for socio-economic development and trade, highlighting Tajikistan's readiness to expand cooperation with international partners and investors.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presents Critical Minerals Development Strategy in Seoul
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Natural Resources, Akyl Toktobaev, presented the country's critical minerals development strategy at the Korea-Central Asia Business Summit in Seoul. He highlighted Kyrgyzstan's resource potential, the need to diversify mining, and invited international cooperation for projects from exploration to processing.

item.title: First Phase of Bishkek Solar Power Plant Launched in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The first phase of the 100-megawatt Bishkek Solar power plant has been launched in Kyrgyzstan's Issyk-Kul region. Implemented with Russian specialists, the project was inaugurated remotely by President Sadyr Japarov. This launch exemplifies successful Russia-Kyrgyz cooperation in the energy sector.

item.title: Printing house banned from selling textbooks to private schools
item.description: The Ministry of Education has prohibited the "Uchkun" printing house from selling textbooks to private educational institutions. The ministry will now collect information from private schools to determine textbook orders. Previously, the printing house sold books without restrictions, as it lacked the right to verify buyers.

item.title: Tajikistan cotton harvest reaches 39,200 tons
item.description: As of September 14, farmers in Tajikistan have harvested 39,190 tons of cotton. Approximately 70,000 pickers are involved in the harvest. Cotton production is a strategic sector for Tajikistan, with a goal of over 394,000 tons by 2026.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host CIS Digitalization and Communications Development Forum
item.description: Dushanbe will host joint meetings of the CIS Communications Administrations Heads Council, CIS Informatization Coordination Council, and ITU Regional Forum on Development for the CIS region from September 29-30, 2026. Discussions will focus on telecommunications, digitalization, cybersecurity, and regional cooperation.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Meets with South Korean National Assembly Speaker
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon met with South Korean National Assembly Speaker Cho Jung-sik in Seoul. They discussed strengthening inter-parliamentary dialogue, economic cooperation, investment, and joint projects, emphasizing the importance of regional stability and development initiatives.

item.title: US Federal Reserve Hikes Interest Rate for First Time in Over Three Years
item.description: The US Federal Reserve raised its key interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 3.75-4%, the first increase since July 2023. Fed Chair Jerome Powell cited persistently high inflation as the reason, noting that underlying inflation trends have not significantly improved. The decision comes amid ongoing cost-of-living pressures for American households.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New Mechanisms to Support Electrotechnical Industry
item.description: Uzbekistan has established new mechanisms to finance working capital, purchase copper raw materials, and attract foreign investors for its electrotechnical industry. Loans of up to $5 million will be available at a 6% annual interest rate with a two-year term, starting October 1, 2026.

item.title: Trump to Discuss Iran Strategy with Gulf Leaders at UN General Assembly
item.description: US President Donald Trump plans to meet with leaders of Persian Gulf countries at the UN General Assembly in New York. The primary topic will be future strategy concerning Iran. The meeting is expected to focus on next steps following the conflict with Tehran, with a plan possibly approved after US midterm elections.

item.title: Trump threatens EU trade halt over Canada rapprochement
item.description: US President Donald Trump criticized the European Commission's proposal to make Canada an associate member of the EU, calling it "ridiculous." He threatened to impose heavy tariffs or completely halt trade with Europe if this move is considered hostile. The European Commission had proposed closer ties with Canada.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea Sign 15 Cooperation Documents
item.description: Tajikistan and South Korea signed 15 new cooperation documents in Seoul on September 16, 2026. Agreements cover customs, intellectual property, education, economy, anti-corruption, financial intelligence, industry, transport, forest restoration, export, labor safety, energy, public service, and law enforcement cooperation.

item.title: Economist: Pension Age or Taxes Must Rise to Balance System
item.description: Economist Otabek Bakirov stated that either the retirement age must be extended or taxes increased to maintain balance in the pension system. He suggested increasing the social tax from 12% to 15% as the easiest option, but considers it unacceptable and incorrect.

item.title: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency to open office in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A representative office of the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) is planned for Kyrgyzstan to support Korean companies. This was announced during a meeting between South Korean National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik and Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. Bilateral trade has doubled, reaching $3.4 billion in 2025.

item.title: UN reports global freshwater reserves are diminishing
item.description: The World Meteorological Organization's report indicates a continuous decline in terrestrial freshwater reserves and retreating glaciers, posing future risks to populations and economies. Rivers worldwide experienced one of the driest periods in over three decades in 2025. The report highlights that the lowest river flow since 1991 was recorded in the past seven years.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan sets fixed prices for beef and mutton to stabilize market
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's antimonopoly service has established fixed prices for beef and mutton to stabilize the market. Prices vary by region, with boneless beef in Bishkek set at 870 soms per kilogram and bone-in beef at 770 soms retail. Wholesale and retail prices for mutton have also been determined across different regions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan presents critical minerals development strategy in Seoul
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Natural Resources, Ecology, and Technical Supervision, Akyl Toktobayev, presented the country's critical minerals development strategy at the Korea-Central Asia Business Summit in Seoul. He highlighted Kyrgyzstan's resource potential and the need to diversify the mining sector, inviting international investment and partnerships.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's processing sector sees significant growth driven by beverages and bread
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's processing sector grew by 8.4% in the first eight months of 2026 compared to the previous year. The beverage and bread industries were key drivers, with turnovers exceeding 20.3 billion soms and a 17.5% increase in bread production. Overall food processing, beverage, and tobacco output reached 81.8 billion soms.

item.title: Dushanbe to host SCO Transport and Logistics exhibition in October
item.description: Dushanbe will host the international exhibition "SCO Transport and Logistics" from October 19-20, coinciding with the 25th anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization. The event aims to showcase the transport and logistics potential of SCO member states and foster cooperation. A working group meeting on transport and logistics will also be held.

item.title: CSTO forces conduct 'Rubezh-2026' exercise in Kazakhstan, practicing combat scenarios
item.description: The second phase of the 'Rubezh-2026' joint exercise for the CSTO Collective Rapid Deployment Forces of the Central Asian region has begun in Kazakhstan. Servicemembers are practicing combat actions, including repelling simulated armed group incursions and clearing explosive devices.

item.title: Tajikistan seeks additional $1 billion for Rogun Dam construction
item.description: Tajikistan plans to raise an additional $1 billion to continue the construction of the Rogun Dam. The funds will be allocated for the completion of the remaining structures on the right bank of the dam.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea's SK Specialty Discuss Tungsten Project
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Industry and New Technologies met with SK Specialty in Seoul to discuss a project for an integrated tungsten value chain. The initiative aims to cover the entire process from mining to production, establishing Tajikistan as a key center for tungsten processing.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Addresses Cooperation with South Korea at Korea University
item.description: During his visit to South Korea, Tajik President Emomali Rahmon spoke at Korea University, expressing gratitude for an honorary doctorate. He highlighted the growth of higher education in Tajikistan, noting an increase in institutions and students, and expressed interest in further academic collaboration with South Korean universities.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korean LS MnM Sign Memorandum on Mining Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Industry and New Technologies, Sherali Kabir, met with LS MnM Inc. leadership in South Korea, signing a memorandum of understanding. The agreement focuses on attracting investment for Tajikistan's mining sector, deep processing of raw materials, and developing value-added products and new processing enterprises.

item.title: Uzbekistan-South Korea Relations Enter New Chapter After Seoul Summit
item.description: Uzbek President's press secretary Sherzod Asadov noted that President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's visit to South Korea was marked by warm meetings and discussions. The South Korean side reportedly showed great respect and attention to the Uzbek president's state visit, heralding a new phase in bilateral relations.

item.title: Concerns Arise Over Textbook Sales Amid Kyrgyzstan's 12-Year Education Transition
item.description: Parents in Kyrgyzstan are complaining about a shortage of new textbooks required for the 12-year education system, forcing them to buy books independently. While officials urge against spreading unverified information and illegal purchases, law enforcement is investigating textbook sales in markets. Significant funds have been allocated for textbook printing.

item.title: SCNS Deputy Chairman Appointed Honorary President of Kyrgyzstan's Judo Federation
item.description: Akylbek Namazov, deputy chairman of Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security, has been appointed Honorary President of the National Judo Federation. Other leadership changes include the appointment of Aitmagomed Ismagombetov as First Vice-President and Emilbek Abdraliev as Vice-President. Kamil Magomedov was introduced as a new national team coach.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes program to fund rural youth university education with regional work commitment
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a program to fund university education for at least five rural youth from each district annually. Graduates must return to their region and work for a minimum of three years after obtaining their diplomas. The program aims to address regional specialist needs, prioritizing fields like medicine, education, and agriculture.

item.title: Taliban seeks Kyrgyzstan's support after joining UN Security Council
item.description: Following Kyrgyzstan's election as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council for 2027-2028, the Taliban government has requested support. The Taliban aims to leverage this position to advance its interests and strengthen political and economic ties with its neighbor.

item.title: Seven children left without parental care returned to Uzbekistan from Russia
item.description: Seven children who were left without parental care in Russia have been returned to Uzbekistan. Measures are being taken to ensure their rights and legal interests, facilitate their return to a family environment, and provide social, medical, and psychological support.

item.title: Uzbekistan Leads CIS Fixed Internet Speed Ranking
item.description: Uzbekistan improved its global Speedtest Global Index ranking in August 2026, rising three positions for both mobile and fixed internet. The country now ranks first in the CIS for fixed internet connection speed. Average mobile download speeds increased to 65.27 Mbps, and fixed speeds rose to 94.50 Mbps.

item.title: EU Pledges Winter Support for Ukraine, Calls for Air Defense
item.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen pledged EU support for Ukraine this winter, anticipating the toughest period since the Russian invasion. The EU plans humanitarian aid, energy supply reinforcement, and enhanced air defense. She urged immediate delivery of US Patriot systems and proposed developing a European, NATO-independent security threat response mechanism.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host Second Presidential Chess Cup
item.description: Dushanbe will host the second Presidential Chess Cup of Tajikistan from November 9 to 17, 2026. The tournament is considered a major Central Asian chess event, attracting grandmasters and young talents. The prize fund is $60,000 USD, with participants competing in two groups based on rating.

item.title: New pediatric intensive care unit opens in Samarkand region hospital
item.description: A six-bed pediatric intensive care unit has opened at the central hospital in Jambay district, Samarkand region. The Public Foundation for Civil Society Support funded the project with 3 billion Uzbek soums, acquiring 39 units of modern medical equipment. This specialized unit will improve healthcare for children in the district.

item.title: New cooperation system aims to boost incomes in Kanlykul district
item.description: Business Development Bank is implementing measures to ensure employment and increase incomes in Kanlykul district. The bank's chairman visited the district, meeting entrepreneurs and reviewing microbusiness projects. An agreement was reached to establish a training center for strawberry cultivation cooperation involving 100 households.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea elevate partnership to new level
item.description: A business forum in Seoul demonstrated a new level of strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and South Korea. President Mirziyoyev outlined economic priorities, calling for investment in new production facilities, technologies, and infrastructure. The goal is to make Uzbekistan a major regional production, technological, and export hub.

item.title: Uzbekistan Ranks First in CIS for Fixed Internet Speed, Mobile Speed Also Increases
item.description: Uzbekistan has become the leader among CIS countries in fixed internet speed. In August, download speeds increased from 62.42 Mbit/s to 65.27 Mbit/s, moving the country from 75th to 72nd globally. Mobile internet speeds also saw growth.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Increases Labor Migration Quota to 120,000 for 2027
item.description: The Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan has raised the quota for labor migrants entering the country to 120,000 for 2027. Previous quotas for 2025 and 2026 were also significantly increased. Countries like China, India, and Turkey are among those requesting quotas.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to remediate sites from former uranium production in Kaji-Sai
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations is preparing to remediate sites left from uranium production in Kaji-Sai village. The work includes dismantling buildings and relocating radioactive waste. Discussions are underway with Rosatom for full remediation of the area around the tailings pond.

item.title: Uzbekistan enacts new law to enhance support for victims of violence
item.description: Uzbekistan's President signed a law on September 11 to improve social services for victims of oppression and violence. The legislation aims to remove practical and administrative barriers, expand legal guarantees, and ensure victims receive qualified state-funded legal aid and social support.
